213200: Lincoln in the Bardo: George Saunders’s Booker Prize–winning novel arrives at the Met in operatic form, with music by American composer Missy Mazzoli and libretto by Royce Vavrek. 213202: Medea: Cherubini’s rarely performed take on classic Greek tragedy stars Sonya Yoncheva as the sorceress whose betrayal drives her to an unthinkable act of revenge. Michael Spyres is Giasone, Medea’s unfaithful Argonaut husband, in David McVicar’s setting of the timeless myth.

213203: Tosca: Searing passion, edge-of-your-seat action, and a career-defining title role: Puccini’s classic thriller follows a jealous diva, the ardent painter who loves her, and the villainous chief of police who tears them asunder in a grand, immersive production by David McVicar set in three picturesque locations in Rome.

213234: Tour With the Curator: Thomas Nast's American Hero: Ulysses S. Grant (1822-1885) was a Civil War hero for the Union and the eighteenth president of the United States of America from 1869-1877. Political cartoonist Thomas Nast (1840-1902) was a supporter and later friend of Grant. MHHM’s newest exhibit in the Nast Gallery and Schoolroom Gallery highlights Grant’s career through artifacts and Nast’s images. This special “behind the scenes” tour blends history with the details of how the exhibit came together.
